podcast.body: Costello's debut single, released on Stiff Records and produced by Nick Lowe. It defined his early sound as melodic but bashing, acerbic but catchy. The song was a diatribe against former British fascist leader Oswald Mosley, whom Costello had seen on TV attempting to distance himself from his racist past. Costello famously began to perform this song live on Saturday Night Live before abruptly switching to another track. "Less than zero was the debut single by the 22-year-old born Declan Patrick McManus known to the world by the moniker Elvis Costello."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.body: This song was Costello's British hit single and was the specific track NBC initially requested him to perform during his appearance on Saturday Night Live on December 17, 1977. However, he ultimately defied their request by playing a different song. "Elvis could have the gig on the condition that he performed his British hit single, which was called Less Than Zero."
